definition: MEAN Security is a core concept in MEAN Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What MEAN Security is
theory.body: MEAN Security describes the methods and patterns used within MEAN Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: MEAN Security is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why MEAN Security matters
theory.body: Without MEAN Security, systems built with MEAN Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How MEAN Security works
theory.body: The mechanism behind MEAN Security follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of MEAN Security.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of MEAN Security
theory.body: MEAN Security offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
